Compute the Leachate Mixing Fraction (LMF) for water quality samples

Source: R/lmf.R
add_lmf.Rd

Appends LMF rows to a long-format water quality dataframe. LMF is a source-detection index estimating what fraction of a sample's chemistry can be attributed to the leachate end-member under a two-component mixing model. See the file-level header for full methodological detail.

Usage

add_lmf(
  df,
  leachate_data = NULL,
  reference_data = NULL,
  lmf_analyte_uuid = NA_character_,
  calibration = c("window", "trailing"),
  calibration_window_years = 5,
  min_leachate_total_n = NULL,
  min_leachate_total_n_units = NULL,
  rsd_default = 0.05,
  min_ref_samples = 10,
  min_leachate_samples = 10,
  max_sigma_lsi = 10,
  max_chi2_per_df = Inf,
  informativeness_threshold = 0.2,
  min_high_info_ions = 3L,
  robust_iterations = 3L,
  robust_threshold_k = 2.5,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

Long-format dataframe. Required columns: sample_id, site_id, analyte, value, detected, datetime, and a unit column (units.analyte or sampleTidy's units). Analyte names may be hydroSense's or sampleTidy's (see analyte_aliases()); valence.analyte and atomic_mass.analyte are optional (see to_meq()). The LMF rows are appended to df as supplied.

leachate_data

Required. Long-format dataframe in the same structure as df providing leachate end-member chemistry. Required columns: sample_id, analyte, value, detected (and datetime for calibration = "trailing"). The total-N quality filter (min_leachate_total_n) applies in both calibration modes: leachate samples below it are ignored. Samples missing the required LMF panel analytes are silently dropped.

reference_data

Required. Long-format dataframe in the same structure as df providing reference site chemistry for end-member calibration. Required columns: sample_id, analyte, value, detected (and datetime for calibration = "trailing"). The same end-member is applied to every site in df.

lmf_analyte_uuid

UUID assigned to LMF rows in the uuid.analyte column of the output. Set to a fixed UUID if integrating with a data system that tracks analytes by UUID. Default NA_character_.

calibration

How the end-members are calibrated. "window" (default) builds one reference and one leachate end-member from all of reference_data / leachate_data, regardless of date, and applies them to every sample. "trailing" calibrates each sample separately, from only the rows of leachate_data and reference_data whose datetime lies in [t - calibration_window_years, t] (inclusive at both ends, where t is the sample's own datetime). Bounds are compared as whole calendar days, each datetime's day taken in its own time zone (UTC when it has none), so clock time never matters. A sample's LMF therefore depends on data up to its own date only, and appending later samples or later end-member data never changes it. A sample whose window has no usable reference or leachate data (none, too few reference samples to estimate spread, too few samples for min_ref_samples or min_leachate_samples, or too few high-information ions) gets an NA LMF with lmf_reason starting "insufficient_calibration_data". "trailing" requires a datetime column in both end-member data frames.

calibration_window_years

Length in years of the trailing calibration window. Used only when calibration = "trailing". Default 5.

min_leachate_total_n

Minimum total N (sum of NH3-N + NO3-N + NO2-N, each converted to mg/L by its row's unit) for a leachate sample to qualify for end-member calibration. Excludes non-representative samples (dilution events, treatment upsets); samples below it do not contribute to the leachate end-member at all. Total N is used rather than NH3-N alone because aerated leachate may have nitrified NH3 to NO3. Numeric or units object; bare numeric requires min_leachate_total_n_units. Default NULL (20 mg/L).

min_leachate_total_n_units

Character unit string for min_leachate_total_n when it is bare numeric, e.g. "mg/L". Ignored when min_leachate_total_n is a units object or NULL.

rsd_default

Default relative analytical uncertainty, applied as sigma_meas = rsd_default * |x| with a floor at rsd_default * |R|. Default 0.05 (5% RSD).

min_ref_samples

Minimum number of reference samples (distinct sample_ids carrying at least one LMF panel ion) in the calibration data – in the sample's trailing window when calibration = "trailing". Below it the LMF is NA with lmf_reason "insufficient_calibration_data". Default 10.

min_leachate_samples

Minimum number of valid leachate samples (total N at least min_leachate_total_n) in the calibration data (in the trailing window for calibration = "trailing"); below it the LMF is NA with lmf_reason "insufficient_calibration_data". Also the number of valid samples with fluoride measured needed for F to join the panel. Default 10.

max_sigma_lsi

Maximum permitted sigma_lmf in percentage points (uncertainty on the mixing fraction estimate). Samples above this threshold return NA with reason code "insufficient_precision". Default 10 (i.e., ±10 percentage points).

max_chi2_per_df

Maximum permitted chi-squared per degree of freedom (computed on the original inverse-variance weights, before robust reweighting). Retained as a diagnostic output in all cases. Default Inf (no hard gate — the robust reweighting handles outlier ions directly, making a hard chi2 gate redundant for most samples).

informativeness_threshold

Threshold on sigma_R / |L - R| for classifying ions as high-information. Computed once from calibration data, not per-sample. Lower values are more stringent. Default 0.20.

min_high_info_ions

Minimum number of high-information ions that must be measured in a sample for LMF to be computed. Samples below this threshold return NA with reason code "insufficient_high_info_ions". Default 3L.

robust_iterations

Number of Huber M-estimator reweighting passes. In each pass, ions whose studentized residuals exceed robust_threshold_k are downweighted proportionally. Three iterations is sufficient for convergence in practice. Set to 0L to disable robust reweighting entirely. Default 3L.

robust_threshold_k

Huber threshold in standard-deviation units on studentized residuals (r_i / sqrt(var_f_i)). Ions with |sr_i| > k have their estimation weight reduced by a factor of k / |sr_i|. Smaller values downweight more aggressively; k = 2.5 is close to the conventional Huber constant. Default 2.5.

verbose

If TRUE, prints an ion informativeness table via cli::cli_inform() showing each ion's score and high/low classification. Useful when tuning informativeness_threshold. Default FALSE.

Value

The input df with LMF rows appended. Each LMF row carries value (the robust LMF estimate as a percentage, 0 = pure reference, 100 = pure leachate), name.analyte = "LMF", uuid.feature (from the input), lmf_naive (the non-robust estimate for comparison), lmf_reason (NA on success, reason code on failure), n_ions_used, n_ions_downweighted (count of ions whose weight was reduced by robust reweighting), n_high_info_downweighted (count of downweighted ions that were high-information tracers; a robust estimate carried by the low-information majority against sensitive tracers signals a mis-attributed source, not a transformation artifact), sigma_lmf, and chi2_per_df (diagnostic; computed on original weights). Columns present in df but not produced by the LMF computation are NA in the appended rows.

References

Christophersen N, Hooper RP (1992) Water Resources Research 28(1):99-107. Christensen JB et al. (2001) Applied Geochemistry 16(7-8):659-718. Kjeldsen P et al. (2002) Crit Rev Environ Sci Technol 32(4).

See also

compute_lmf_for_sample, to_meq, analyte_aliases

Examples

# \donttest{
# Quantify each downstream sample's leachate-mixing fraction from its
# major-ion signature, calibrated against the leachate and reference
# end-members in the bundled demo data.
demo <- leachate_demo()
out <- add_lmf(
  df             = subset(demo, site_id == "downstream"),
  leachate_data  = subset(demo, site_id == "leachate"),
  reference_data = subset(demo, site_id == "reference"),
  # the demo has 6 samples per end-member; the defaults ask for 10
  min_ref_samples      = 5,
  min_leachate_samples = 5
)
subset(out, analyte == "LMF", c("sample_id", "value"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   sample_id value
#>   <chr>     <dbl>
#> 1 DS-01      15.0
#> 2 DS-02      14.8
#> 3 DS-03      14.7
#> 4 DS-04      14.9
#> 5 DS-05      14.7
#> 6 DS-06      14.9
# }
